meta.title: Waves — split the flat's bills, skip the awkward asking
meta.description: Waves tracks every shared expense, works out who owes whom, nudges flatmates for you, and opens UPI with the exact amount. Capture expenses from bank SMS on Android or by voice, and keep going with the network off. Free, with no limit on groups or expenses.
meta.ogAlt: Waves — split the flat's bills, skip the awkward asking

banner.text: The whole ledger is free. No card, no trial clock.

custody.claim: Waves never holds, moves, or touches your money.
custody.body: It works out who pays whom, hands the amount to the payment app you already use — UPI first — and records what both sides agreed. That is why there is nothing here for anyone to run off with.

features.title: Built around the part that goes wrong
features.subtitle: Splitting is the easy half. Waves is designed for the other half — remembering, reconciling, and asking for the money so you don't have to.

items.title: Your bank's SMS becomes an expense
items.body: On Android, Waves reads the transaction SMS your bank already sends and turns it into a draft expense — amount, merchant and date filled in — so you confirm it and pick who shares it, instead of typing it from memory at the end of the month.
points: Android only, for now
Amount, merchant and date pre-filled
You confirm each draft before it counts
Works with the SMS your bank already sends

items.title: Say it. Don't type it.
items.body: Hold the microphone and say "cook three fifty" or "twelve fifty for coffee, split with Arjun" — the expense arrives filled in, ready to check before it is saved. Prefer paper? Point the camera at a receipt and Waves itemises it on the device.
points: Several expenses in one breath
"Three fifty" is read as 350, "2k" as 2,000
Flatmates' names matched even when you say them loosely
Receipt scanning that itemises the bill

items.title: One tap to UPI, with the exact amount
items.body: Waves works out who owes whom, reduces it to the fewest payments that clear it, and opens your UPI app with the exact amount ready. Pay part of it, attach the proof, and either side can reject a settlement that never happened. Waves never touches the money.
points: Opens UPI with the exact amount
The fewest payments that settle the flat
Partial and per-expense settlements
Attach proof; either side can cancel or reject

items.title: Polite reminders, sent for you
items.body: When a flatmate still owes, Waves nudges them on your behalf, with the amount, so you don't have to bring it up over dinner or in the group chat.
points: Reminders go out for you, not from you
Each one carries the exact amount owed
Balances stay up to date as expenses sync
A full edit history, so nobody argues from memory

items.title: Every kind of split, none of the arithmetic
items.body: Equal, exact amounts, shares, percentages, or one person covering someone else. Waves keeps the remainder honest — the split always adds back to the bill, to the last minor unit, because amounts are stored as whole paise and cents rather than as decimals.
points: Equal, exact, shares and percentage splits
Split one bill between two groups of people
Comment on any expense when the memory gets fuzzy
Recurring bills that reset every month

items.title: Add an expense with no network at all
items.body: Waves writes to your phone first and syncs later. A basement flat with no signal, a flight, a mountain road — none of it stops the ledger. The copy on your device is encrypted at rest, and signing out destroys the key.
points: Everything works with the network off
Conflict-safe sync when you come back
Encrypted at rest on your device
Sign out and the local copy becomes unreadable

how.title: Three steps, then it gets out of the way

steps.title: Start a flat, share the link
steps.body: A flat, a trip, a dinner, or one person. Send the link or show the QR code — flatmates can join and see the group in a browser, without an account and without installing anything.

steps.title: Add what you spend
steps.body: Type it, say it, scan the receipt, or let the bank SMS fill it in on Android. Waves splits it the way you asked and updates everyone's balance the moment it syncs — or the moment you are back on a network.

steps.title: Settle up without the awkward asking
steps.body: Waves works out who owes whom, nudges flatmates for you, opens UPI with the exact amount filled in, and marks it settled once both sides agree.

privacy.title: What Waves can and cannot see
privacy.body: Most apps in this category tell you they take privacy seriously. Here is the same claim written as three lists, including the one nobody publishes.

cant.title: Your money
cant.body: Waves never holds, moves or touches funds. Settling hands off to your own payment app, so there is no balance here to see.

cant.title: The ledger on your device
cant.body: The local copy is encrypted at rest with a key held in your phone's own keystore. It never leaves the device, and signing out destroys it.

cant.title: Your receipts, if you say so
cant.body: Photos can stay on the device, or go to your own Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive. Not to us.

does.title: The shared ledger
does.body: Groups, expenses, splits and settlements are on our server, because that is what lets four phones agree. Everyone in a group can already see all of it.

does.title: An account
does.body: An email address or the identifier your sign-in provider gives us, plus which devices you use, so a stolen session can be revoked.

does.title: No data sales
does.body: No advertising, no data sales, no tracking for anyone else's benefit. The free tier is paid for by the paid tier.

wont.title: The people you split with
wont.body: Everyone in a group can see that group's expenses, amounts and comments. Privacy here means privacy from us and from outsiders, not from the group.

wont.title: Losing the device before it syncs
wont.body: An expense that has not synced exists only in the encrypted copy on that phone. If the phone is gone before it reaches the server, so is the expense.

wont.title: Anything on the server side, from us
wont.body: The shared ledger is not end-to-end encrypted. We could technically read it, we have no reason to, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise.

privacy.footnote: Waves has not been through an independent security audit, and this page will say so until it has. Deleting your account deletes the rows, not a flag on a row we keep.

items.a: Yes. Groups, people, expenses, currencies, offline use and settling up are unlimited on the free tier. Plus exists for the features with a running cost behind them — receipt scanning, photo storage and extra devices. There is no card at sign-up and no trial that expires.

items.q: Does everyone need to install the app?
items.a: No. Share a link or a QR code and people can join and see the group in a browser, with no account and no download. They can create an account later if they want the app, and the ledger follows them.

items.q: What happens when I have no signal?
items.a: Adding, editing and splitting keep working. Waves writes every expense to your phone first, so none of it needs the network. When you reconnect it syncs in the background and reconciles anything that changed while you were away.

items.q: Does Waves work with more than one currency?
items.a: Yes. Every amount is stored in the currency it was spent in, as whole minor units rather than as a decimal, so nothing drifts. You can fix the exchange rate you actually got for one bill, for one person, or for a whole trip, and every ISO 4217 currency is supported.

No, and that is deliberate. Waves works out who pays whom and how much, then hands that to a payment app you already use — a bank transfer, UPI, Pix, SEPA, PayNow, Venmo, PayPal or cash. Your money never passes through us, and Waves is not a bank.

items.q: What do you do with my data?
items.a: As little as we can. The ledger on your device is encrypted at rest, receipt photos can stay on your device or in your own cloud storage, and there is no advertising and no data selling. The shared ledger is on our server because that is what lets several phones agree — it is not end-to-end encrypted, and we would rather say so plainly.

Waves is not tied to a payment network or a banking licence, so there is nothing to roll out country by country — you can use it wherever you can install the app or open the web app. UPI settle-up is built for India, and other payment apps work the same way: Waves hands over the amount and you pay.
